items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S3405

SPONSOR: KENNEDY
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the transportation law, in relation to procurement of
contract proposals for zero-emission buses

 
PURPOSE:

This bill would require public transportation systems in their evalu-
ation of ,procurement contract proposals for the purchase of zero-emis-
sion buses and charging equipment to use a system that incorporates a
best-value contracting framework. Such framework shall prioritize
proposed contracts that include: an employment plan (which shall include
worker wages, benefits, a commitment., to create jobs for under repres-
ented individuals, etc.), a commitment to consider the community that
surrounds such offeror's facility and a description of efforts by the
offeror to mitigate its impact on climate change.

 
SUMMARY OF SPECIFIC PROVISIONS:

Section one, subdivision one requires that the evaluation process for
procurement contract proposals for the purchase of zero-emission busses
and charging equipment include a "best-value" framework. A best-value
framework is one that prioritizes proposed contracts that include: an
employment plan (which shall include worker wages, benefits, a commit-
ment to create jobs for under represented individuals, etc.), a commit-
ment to consider the community that surrounds such offeror's facility
and a description of, efforts by the offeror to mitigate its impact on
climate change.

Section one, subdivision two establishes that a notice must be provided
to offerors stating that information related to employment and other
reports are Subject to disclosure under the Freedom of Information Law,
and that the final contract and compliance documents. shall be made
available to the public Online.ò

Section one, subdivision four states that the section shall be subject
to the provisions of section one hundred thirty-nine-i of the state
finance law ,- *Lich pertains to notifying and encouraging the use of
New York, state subcontractors.

Section one, Subdivision five states that the Department of Transporta-
tion Shall promulgate regulations to establish the forms, manner and
process by Which offerors shall submit contract proposals pursuant to
this section.

Section one, subdivision six states that public transportation systems
that enter into a contract for zero emission buses shall issue quarterly
report's to the commissioner for the first year of the contract and
annually thereafter to the commissioner and elected officials section
two sets forth that that the provisions of this act shall be severable.

Section three sets forth the effective date.

 
JUSTIFICATION:


Over the past eight years, 11 procurements by four transit agencies have
utilized an evaluation processes for suppliers and procurement contracts
that have secured the creation of over 1,030 direct jobs and supported
thousands more throughout the supply chain. From the Northeast Corridor
to the West Coast, labor requirements and employment plans similar to
the provisions of this bill have been included in over $7 billion worth
of transportation projects.

In a 2016 RFP, the Metropolitan Transportation Authority required a
range of employment opportunities to be created and retained in
connection with the production, delivery, testing, and warranty coverage
requirements of the contract to be included in bids.  Offerors were also
required to describe the direct dollar value and the fringe benefit
costs for those jobs, and the commitment the offeror would make to
achieve that level of job creation/retention. The $3.7 billion contract
for 1,612 subway cars was awarded to Kawasaki Rail Car to manufacture
cars in both Yonkers, NY and Lincoln, NE. The contract also contained a
plan to increase and retain employment at for Alstom, a major supplier
in Hornell and Rochester, NY. This legislation would ensure that our
move towards a pollution-free transportation system also supports
sustainable labor practices.

 
LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

2020: S.8548 Referred to Transportation, A.10559 Referred to RO.PS

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

Undetermined.

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect immediately.

summary: Requires a best-value contracting framework when evaluating procurement contract proposals for zero-emission buses and charging equipment.
